title: Nike Gyakusou Returns to Challenge What Performance Running Looks Like Next
summary: For 16 years, Nike Gyakusou has brought a new design language to performance running, pairing Nike innovation with Jun Takahashi’s perspective as both a designer and runner. Now, with its first collection since 2021, Gyakusou is building on that very foundation, bringing forward new ideas in performance, function and design.
body_markdown:
For 16 years, Nike Gyakusou has brought a new design language to performance running, pairing Nike innovation with Jun Takahashi’s perspective as both a designer and runner. Now, with its first collection in more than half a decade, Gyakusou is building on that very foundation, bringing forward new ideas in performance, function and design.


Gyakusou, which translates to “running in reverse” in Japanese, has never separated how running product performs from how it looks. Function and design have shaped one another from the beginning. That differentiated point of view gave people another way into running and continues to shape running culture today.


“Running culture has evolved since we started Gyakusou, and the sport is much bigger,” says Takahashi. “The philosophy behind Gyakusou feels especially relevant now as a new generation are finding their own reasons to run and express themselves through running.”


When Gyakusou launched in 2010, performance running had a more uniform aesthetic. Gyakusou introduced unexpected approaches to color, construction and utility while remaining grounded in the needs of runners. Rather than recreate what made it distinctive in the past, Gyakusou’s first new collection since 2021 takes the same instinct to challenge convention and applies it to performance running today.


Built for cold-weather running, the collection uses Nike performance innovation to address where runners need warmth, protection, breathability and freedom of movement. Lightweight down jackets and vests feature Nike AeroLoft bonded insulation and water-repellent materials to provide warmth and protection without compromising mobility. Performance running tights and pants deliver flexibility and support for every stride, while GIRA running T-shirts and gloves complete an apparel system designed around the needs of runners braving the elements.


The footwear brings the same balance of performance and expression across different running experiences. The[Nike Alphafly 4](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-alphafly-4-helps-more-runners-go-the-distance-with-speed-and-confidence) SP helps runners carry speed over the marathon distance, and the[Nike Vomero Plus](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-vomero-plus-vomero-premium-official-images) SP brings maximum cushioning to everyday miles.


Previously known for unexpected palettes, Gyakusou challenges that history this season by stripping color back. Tonal whites bring a stark simplicity, while earthy greens reconnect the collection to the natural world.


Nike and Takahashi are inviting a new generation to experience the Gyakusou philosophy, creating space for new running perspectives while carrying forward its more expansive approach to the sport.


The 2026 Gyakusou Collection launches December 3 at Undercover stores,[undercoverism.com](https://undercoverism.com/) and Dover Street Market London, as well as at the Shanghai Marathon Expo and Shanghai Nike Running and NikeLab stores. The collection releases globally December 11 at[nike.com](https://www.nike.com/) ,[SNKRS](https://www.nike.com/launch) and select retail locations.
